_changelogNote: There is no CHANGELOG.md in this repository — the changelog lives only in src/data/changelog.ts, rendered by src/app/changelog/page.tsx. So there is no markdown surface to check package.json against, and the `changelog` key is deliberately absent. Instead src/guards/changelog-renders.test.ts asserts that the newest entry matches APP_VERSION, which the version-surface check above ties back to package.json. Note this file's section key is `heading`, where every other app in the suite uses `title` — do not copy a sibling guard without adjusting.
_claudeMdNote: Swept on 2026-07-30. The `**Version:** X.Y.Z` line is the only version declaration; the other X.Y.Z mentions are historical prose ('v2.5.6 cleared nine GHSAs') and are correct as written — never flag those. Skipped in CI, where this gitignored file is not checked out.
_gitBaseBranchNote: Consumed by TWO scripts at two different moments, and the split is the point. shipgate.mjs uses it PRE-merge for one assertion only — that this clone is not BEHIND origin/<branch>, i.e. the release is being cut on top of current main. verify-sync.mjs uses it POST-merge for the three-way SHA comparison (local, remote-tracking, GitHub API) plus a clean-tree check. Neither check can live in the other's moment: the gate runs partway through a release with the version and changelog edits UNCOMMITTED, so a clean-tree assertion there would fail every release; and the post-merge SHA condition does not exist yet when the gate runs. Both self-skip under CI: actions/checkout is shallow and detached, so origin/<branch> is not a meaningful local ref there, and a CI runner has no view of a developer's clone at all — which is why this drift was invisible to every mechanism the suite already had. Remove this key to disable both checks; the gate then prints nothing for them rather than passing silently.

commands.name: check:pointers (register cross-repo cells)
commands._note: Resolves every `path:symbol` in allowlist-contracts.ts `source`/`minSource` at that entry's own sourceCommit, in the sibling checkouts under ~/Developer, and meters how stale each cited file is. ⚠️ WHAT ITS GREEN DOES AND DOES NOT PROVE, stated here so the limit survives someone reading this gate without running it: IN CI THE SIBLING REPOSITORIES ARE NOT CHECKED OUT, so every repo-scoped row is a declared skip, the command checks ZERO of 26 cells and exits 0. That green proves nothing about the register. It prints `SCOPE checked N of 26 cells` on EVERY run, green or red, precisely so an empty pass is never mistaken for a clean one. Enforcement is therefore LOCAL PRE-FLIGHT only — which for a one-committer suite is the real enforcement point. The proof that the checker still DISCRIMINATES is src/guards/pointer-check-discriminates.test.ts, which builds its own throwaway git repository and so runs in CI and cannot skip. Added in 2.5.31, once that self-test existed: wiring it in beforehand would have converted a script with one demonstrated live failure into one that had never been observed to fail.

commands.name: test:rules (Firestore rules vs emulator)
commands._note: Runs the REAL firestore.rules against the Firestore emulator. This is the guard on LIST-1 (2026-08-19): every *_projects collection had shipped `allow list: if isAuth();`, letting any authenticated SPERT user list every project in the suite. It asserts BOTH directions — the unfiltered list is denied AND each of the seven apps' actual production queries still return their documents, checked down to document ids. A rule loosened again fails it; so does one tightened past an app's own query, which would black out project loading for all seven apps. Deliberately NOT in `npm test`: that suite must stay runnable with no emulator. Needs firebase-tools (a pinned devDependency here, so `npm ci` supplies the CLI) and a JRE (ubuntu-latest has one; scripts/run-rules-tests.mjs resolves Homebrew's keg-only JDK on macOS and EXITS NON-ZERO if it finds none — it never skips). No change to .github/workflows/shipgate.yml, which stays byte-identical across all nine repos.

commands.name: functions — install
commands._note: REQUIRED, and easy to miss. functions/ is a separate package with its own manifest and node_modules. The CI workflow runs `npm ci` at the ROOT only, so without this step the functions build fails in CI with `Cannot find type definition file for 'jest'` while passing locally, where functions/node_modules already exists. Putting it here rather than in the workflow keeps .github/workflows/shipgate.yml byte-identical across all nine repos — repo-specific detail belongs in this file.

commands.name: functions — lint
commands._note: functions/ predates the suite's move to Vitest and stays on Jest — two runners in one repository is deliberate, and they never interact.

commands.name: functions — test (jest)
commands._note: Includes aiOpContractHash.test.ts, which pins the cross-repo digest of ai-op-contract.json. SPERT Scheduler pins the same constant in src/integration/ai-op-contract-hash.test.ts, so a one-sided edit to the contract now fails in the repo where it was made.
